description: Je suis Sokhna Maï Mbacké Fall, étudiante en ingénierie électromécanique à l’ESP de Dakar, passionnée d'aérospatial. Je lance LunaForge : L’équipe est déjà composée de profils très intéressants. Nous recherchons principalement un profil en game design / UI-UX, sciences spatiales/physique ou analyse et visualisation de données pour compléter l’équipe.
summary:
LunaForge is an interactive educational simulator designed to conceptualize, assemble, and validate the technical architecture of space missions. Due to the high complexity of aerospace engineering, students and enthusiasts often lack accessible tools that demonstrate the real-world interdependencies between spacecraft subsystems.
The platform addresses this challenge by combining a catalog of technical components (structure, electrical power, telecommunications, scientific instruments, propulsion) with a 3D assembly studio and a real-time calculation engine. Each selected part is linked to a parameterized datasheet (mass, cost, power consumption, nominal voltage, reliability). The simulator automatically verifies geometric alignment, mechanical and electrical interfaces, and overall mission feasibility. By translating complex engineering constraints into clear, educational diagnostics, LunaForge demystifies NASA mission design workflows and promotes hands-on STEM learning.
details:
• How it works
    Project LunaForge is structured around three core modules: a subsystem-based component catalog, a 3D assembly studio, and a technical analysis dashboard. Users select hardware equipped with defined physical and electrical properties and mount them onto a spacecraft bus using a progressive workflow (guided slots transitioning to semi-free placement). A real-time validation engine checks for geometric collisions, interface compatibility, and overall system budgets (mass, cost, power, communications) before generating a comprehensive mission feasibility report.
  • Benefits and expected impact
    The platform turns abstract systems engineering principles into a tangible, visual experience. Users immediately observe the cascading effects of design trade-offs, such as how adding a scientific payload alters power requirements and total launch mass. The expected impact is to lower the barrier to entry for aerospace systems engineering and inspire students to pursue careers in STEM fields.
  • Tools, programming languages, and resources used
    The software architecture decouples technical data from 3D assets to ensure easy scalability of the component library. Development utilizes an interactive 3D rendering environment paired with an analytical calculation engine built with JavaScript/TypeScript and Python for physical budget modeling. Engineering rules and baseline parameters are grounded in official NASA resources, including the Design and Develop a Science Mission framework and the General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT).
  • Creativity and key factors considered
    The core innovation lies in enforcing strict engineering realism over purely visual building: a visually assembled spacecraft will fail validation with actionable educational feedback if electrical or mass constraints are violated. Key factors considered include data-driven modularity, beginner-friendly error diagnostics, progressive difficulty levels, and adherence to authentic space mission design standards.
